title: Bengals may have been robbed twice by refs in final five seconds of stunning loss to Commanders - CBS Sports
description: The Monday night matchup seemed to end with two botched situations from the officials
body:
The Monday night matchup seemed to end with two botched situations from the officials
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:52 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Washington Commanders pulled off a stunner on Monday night with a 22-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals that wasn't decided until Drew Stevens hit a 26-yard field goal on a final play that probably shouldn't have been the final play. The officiating crew appeared to make at least two mistakes in the final five seconds, both of which went against the Bengals, and one of them involved the clock. When a kicker is attempting a field goal in the NFL, the clock is supposed to stop as soon as the ball hits the net (or the ground). On the Commanders' game-winning kick, there were four seconds left when the ball was snapped, and there appeared to be two seconds left when the ball hit the net. The clock somehow ran down to zero after Drew Stevens' game-winning field goal.  Now, in fairness to the clock operator, the time left on the clock went down from two seconds to one second right when the ball hit the net, so stopping it with at least one second left is almost certainly what should have happened here. Instead, the clock operator let the time run out. 
It's pretty clear that there should have been at least one second left, but under NFL rules, the officials aren't allowed to add any time in a situation like this. ESPN rules analyst Russell Yurk broke down the situation on the broadcast. "The clock ran to zero, but there were still two seconds left when the ball hit the net," Yurk said. "So, by rule, there were two seconds left, but replay cannot restore time when there are two seconds or more if the next snap is anything other than a scrimmage snap. So because the next snap would have been a kickoff, they cannot, by rule, put time back on the clock. So it properly ended."Yurk is essentially admitting that there should have been time left, but the NFL rulebook doesn't allow the ref to put that time back on in this specific situation. 
"In a perfect world, the clock operator should stop the clock when the ball hits the net, and there would be two seconds left for a kickoff," Yurk said. "But once it ran to zero, there's nothing replay can do to fix it."If the Bengals had been given the extra second, they would have only had time for one play. That play would likely have been the ensuing kickoff, but if no time went off the clock on the kickoff, then Cincinnati's offense would have time for one last-ditch effort. At that point, the Bengals would have had a chance to throw a Hail Mary, which is an extremely low-percentage play, but anything can happen on a Hail Mary — just ask the Commanders about that. 
Not to mention, the Bengals have two of the best receivers in the league in Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase, so a Hail Mary would have certainly added some intrigue to the end of the game. 
This situation isn't going to come up very often, but it seems like the NFL should have a rule in place to prevent something like this from happening in the future. Questionable call No. 2One play before Stevens kicked his game-winning field goal, there was another questionable call, which the officiating crew also appeared to botch. With the Commanders trailing 20-19 in the final minute, Jayden Daniels made some huge plays to get them in field goal range. The biggest one came on a 42-yard pass to Antonio Williams that brought the Commanders down to the Bengals' 8-yard line. At that point, the Commanders didn't have any timeouts, so they hurried down the field so they could spike the ball to stop the clock. 
Washington ended up spiking the ball with five seconds left in the game, but the problem is that the Commanders' offense may have been lined up in an illegal formation. The Commanders don't appear to have seven guys on the line of scrimmage.  
                                                                    ESPN/NFL
                                                            In the NFL, you have to have seven guys on the line of scrimmage for each play, and you could certainly argue that's not the case for the Commanders here. The receiver at the top should have been on the line of scrimmage at the 8-yard line, but he appears to be about 1.5 yards off the line. This isn't as clear-cut as the clock incident, but the Commanders probably should have been flagged here. That would NOT be a 10-second runoff, but it would have moved Washington's game-winning field-goal attempt back five yards. 
That might not seem like much, but Stevens' kick was veering left the whole way, and it almost certainly would have missed it if it had been attempted from 31 yards instead of 26. This kick probably doesn't make it from 31 yards away.  It was a windy night, and Stevens is a rookie kicker, so adding five yards to the attempt would have certainly been a big deal. Of course, both of these non-calls went against the Bengals, who will probably be making a complaint or two to the NFL this week. Despite the bad calls, the Commanders certainly did enough to earn the win, especially in the second half, when they scored on all five of their offensive possessions.

title: LSU's MiLaysia Fulwiley returns to Tigers, puts up 14 points in first game back after felony charges dropped - CBS Sports
description: Fulwiley still faces three misdemeanor charges after allegedly hitting a police officer with a vehicle
body:
Fulwiley still faces three misdemeanor charges after allegedly hitting a police officer with a vehicle
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:24 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LSU star MiLaysia Fulwiley returned to action on Monday after her felony charges were dropped, and scored 14 points off the bench in a 103-45 win over Belmont. Fulwiley missed the Tigers' last two games after she was arrested on Nov. 14 for allegedly hitting a police officer with a vehicle. Fulwiley, who received a standing ovation from the crowd when she checked in, added three assists, five steals and three blocks in 17 minutes as the Tigers moved to 7-0 with another dominant victory. "Our basketball team was so excited to see her back in the locker room," LSU coach Kim Mulkey said after the game. "She just picked up tonight kind of where she left off, except for a few moments there where she got a little bit winded."
Fulwiley was booked on five counts, including aggravated assault and aggravated battery, both of which were felonies. The felony charges have since been dropped, East Baton Rouge District Attorney Hillar Moore told WAFB, but Fulwiley is still facing three misdemeanors for flight from an officer, resisting an officer and disobedience to an officer.The Louisiana State Police released a statement regarding the change in charges:
"As with all arrests and investigations, the circumstances and evidence surrounding criminal charges are subject to review by the appropriate District Attorney's Office.After a thorough review with all involved parties, the charges were amended based on the circumstances and evidence presented.Louisiana State Police remains committed to ensuring that all incidents are thoroughly documented, evidence is carefully reviewed, and cases are handled in coordination with the appropriate prosecutorial authorities. This matter was handled in accordance with the same investigative standards and procedures applied to countless other cases."Fulwiley also released a statement regarding the incident:"Saturday night ended in a situation that never should have happened, and my posts afterward made it worse. For that, I owe an apology to the officers involved and everyone who calls themselves a Tiger. I also want to apologize to my family and all those who love and support me. People see the purple and gold before they see me, and I want to carry myself in a way that's worthy of it, on the court and off."Rules and laws apply to everyone, including the instructions of officers working a game night in Baton Rouge. I respect the job those officers do, and I'll let the legal process run its course. My focus is doing what this program asks of me and earning back the trust of the people who count on me."Fulwiley transferred to LSU in 2025 after playing her first two collegiate seasons at South Carolina, where she won a national championship as a freshman. She is the reigning back-to-back SEC Sixth Player of the Year and is currently projected as a top 10 pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft. It's unclear how, or if, this incident will affect her standing with WNBA teams. Through her first five games this season, Fulwiley is averaging 17 points, three rebounds, four assists, 4.4 steals and 2.2 blocks on 53.1% shooting. Her return will be a big boost to the Tigers as their schedule starts to ramp up following a very easy start to the season. LSU is 7-0 and ranked No. 9 in the country, but has played every game at home and hasn't faced an opponent in the top 100 in the Bart Torvik rankings. In fact, Belmont, which checks in at No. 135, was the Tigers' toughest opponent yet. LSU's 109-point win over Texas Southern was the largest in Division I history, and the Tigers have won their first seven games by an average of 69.4 points.

body:
The Dawgs have separated from the pack with four dominant wins over ranked foes, while inconsistency continues to define the rest of the field
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:06 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Georgia is pulling away.The story of this season has been parity. For the most part, the new world of college football, with NIL and the transfer portal, has helped to spread the figurative wealth as teams spend the literal kind. However, while that parity holds true, it's hard to ignore what Georgia has done over the last month compared to its competition.After a huge win at Alabama on Oct. 10, the Bulldogs let go of the rope against Auburn. A poor performance in which the Dawgs repeatedly turned the ball over led to their only loss of the season, a 27-24 defeat to the Tigers. Since then, we've seen a re-focused Georgia team.They've reeled off four straight wins against ranked opponents, outscoring them 181-42. And while they've done this, everybody else has played at the same inconsistent speed we've seen from everybody all year. As a result, Georgia has been pulling away from everybody else in my ratings for a while, and this week the gap widened even more.Now, as we approach the final weekend of the regular season, I have Georgia a full 5.5 points better than everybody else in the country. Its rating has not reached the heights it reached between 2021 and 2023, but while these Dawgs may not be the elite team of the past that felt like it was playing a different sport, they are playing the sport better than anybody else right now. So much so that the 5.5-point gap that separates Georgia from Notre Dame at No. 2 is nearly the same gap (5.2) that separates No. 2 Notre Dame from No. 9 Tennessee.Which is not to say Georgia will win the national title. Winning three difficult games is still winning three difficult games, and one bad decision can end your season when it's win-or-go-home. But I wouldn't want to pick anybody else right now.Title odds via DraftKings
Fornelli Power Ratings1
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Georgia
                    
    
    When trying to figure out what's so different about this year's Georgia compared to last year, it's the lines of scrimmage in my eyes. They block well in the run game and keep heat off of  Gunner Stockton  when he drops back to pass. On the other side, a Georgia defense that finished last season ranked 116th nationally (you read that right) in pressure rate ranks eighth this season. Last Week: 1 | Title Odds: +1902
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Notre Dame
                    
    
    The Irish won again and climbed to No. 2 this week, but they continue to suffer injuries. This week it's safety  Luke Talich  who has been lost for the season with a torn Achilles. He's the team's leading tackler, but only because their prior leading tackler,  Drayk Bowen , has been out since suffering an injury against  Navy . They've been able to survive the losses against their current schedule, but I can't help but believe it'll be a much bigger issue in a playoff game. Last Week: 3 | Title Odds: +3903
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Miami (Fla.)
                    
    
    I don't know if  Miami  was taking  Virginia Tech  for granted on Saturday night, but that was a rather disappointing performance. The Hokies had just allowed  Stanford  to put up 40 points on them, but held the Canes to 28 while holding Miami's run game in check and forcing two interceptions from  Darian Mensah  in what was, statistically, his worst performance of the season. Last Week: 2 | Title Odds: +11004
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Texas
                    
    
    Saturday was just what was prescribed for the Longhorns and their fans. Considering the wars this team has found itself in all year,  you can't ask for much more from Senior Day than an easy 45-3 win over an  Arkansas  team that looked overwhelmed from the jump. You'd like to think  Texas A&M  on Friday will be just as easy, but, well, rivalry games on a short week can be tricky. Last Week: 5 | Title Odds: +6505
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Alabama
                    
    
    Alabama's rating suffered slightly this week because their opponent adjusted metrics all regressed for the second-straight week. I still think it's a very good team, and one that's capable of winning it all when it plays at its best level. Last Week: 4 | Title Odds: +6006
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Oregon
                    
    
    Georgia is my pick to win it all, but  Oregon  is my pick to be the Cinderella story of the tournament if it manages to work its way into the field. The Ducks are certainly doing everything they need to grab an at-large bid, showing no mercy against opponents. They then watched the Big Ten fall into chaos on Saturday, opening up many possible paths to the Big Ten Championship. Last Week: 8 | Title Odds: +22007
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Utah
                    
    
    Don't be overly fooled by the 38-17 score in  Utah's  win at  TCU . It was a 17-17 game halfway through the fourth quarter before a three-touchdown barrage put the game away. At this point, it seems the only real question about the Utes is whether they win out and get a bye, or trip up and find themselves hosting a first-round game. Last Week: 7 | Title Odds: +29008
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Wake Forest
                    
    
    The Wagon keeps rolling. The Deacs simply roll out of bed every morning, and there's already 40 points on the board against you. Yes, the schedule has been Charmin soft for nearly two months, but they are absolutely eviscerating teams. This week's closer against  Duke  will be their toughest test in a while, though. Last Week: 10 | Title Odds: +22009
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Tennessee
                    
    
    Unless the Vols figure out a way to get blown out by  Vanderbilt  this week, they should be in the field. As I've mentioned before, my questions about their limitations on offense make me highly skeptical that this team could win enough playoff games to take home the national title, but the defense is so damned good that I can't rule it out entirely. I feel bad for any team that might have to head to Knoxville for a playoff game. Last Week: 11 | Title Odds: +200010
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Indiana
                    
    
    The lack of a reliable offense finally caught up to the Hoosiers on Saturday night in Seattle.  Indiana  benched  Grant Wilson  for  Josh Hoover , but aside from the fact that they wear different numbers, both looked exactly the same. The run game is inconsistent, which often puts them behind the chains, and neither QB is reliable enough to get them out of trouble on obvious passing downs. It isn't likely to hurt them against  Purdue , but how confident are you that this team will win a playoff game if it makes the field? Last Week: 6 | Title Odds: +230011
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Ohio State
                    
    
    There's a cruel irony in the fact that the Buckeyes played their best offensive game with  Luke Fahey  at QB (who played his best game as a Buckeye), and  Ohio State  scored more points against  Nebraska  than any other team this season, and the Buckeyes lost anyway. Their conference title and national title hopes are over, and this is a failure of a season, but they are still one of the 12 best teams in the country from a power-rating standpoint. Last Week: 12 | Title Odds: Off the board12
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Texas Tech
                    
    
    I was waiting for the  Thomas Castellanos  letdown game. He's been playing this sport for five years, and you know that he's incapable of just playing well for long stretches of time. He was overdue, and it came against  Baylor , but guess what? Tech won anyway. Its defense played a great game a week after looking strong against  Oklahoma State  too. While Utah is the best team in the Big 12,  Texas Tech  might be playing the best football in the Big 12 right now. That may set up for a very interesting Big 12 Championship should the Red Raiders avoid a Castellanos catastrophe (a Castastrophe?) against TCU. Last Week: 11 | Title Odds: +7000Dropped out: LSU

        The first bowl game ever played in Puerto Rico will be broadcast nationally on CBS Sports Network on Dec. 16.The inaugural TransPerfect San Juan Bowl, an ACC vs. Sun Belt matchup, will kick off on CBS Sports Network at 7:30 p.m. ET, it was announced Tuesday. The game will also stream on the CBS Sports app.The Sun Belt has long sought a guaranteed bowl matchup against a power-conference opponent, and it got one in October when the bowl game was announced. Participating teams will be announced once matchups are finalized on Dec. 6.The TransPerfect San Juan Bowl will be played inside Hiram Bithorn Stadium, built as a baseball venue and home to events from the World Baseball Classic, Major League Baseball and international soccer. TransPerfect is a language and AI services company, which previously served as the title sponsor of the Music City Bowl from 2020 through 2024. In addition to being the San Juan Bowl's title sponsor, the company also owns the bowl game.
"We're thrilled to partner with CBS Sports to air the inaugural TransPerfect San Juan Bowl," TransPerfect president and co-CEO Phil Shawe said in a statement. "The importance of bringing American football to the Latino community is underscored by this past weekend's NFL game in Mexico City—and we are proud to play a small role in that endeavor. Further, we expect to showcase Puerto Rico's unique appeal with cultural events surrounding the game, including musical performances by well-known local artists."
        
            
                Bowl projections: Slotting all 47 games as Week 12 upsets provide massive shakeup to postseason picture
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Two bowl games will be played in Puerto Rico in December. The Sanders Grossman Law Puerto Rico Bowl will debut Dec. 22 in Bayamón with a MAC team facing an FBS opponent to be determined. CBS Sports is the broadcast partner for two bowl games this season: the San Juan Bowl on CBS Sports Network and the Sun Bowl, a CBS fixture since 1968.
CBS Sports Network reaches about 61 million television households in the U.S.

Sullivan joins Antoine Griezmann on this season's award list as MLS continues to hand out postseason honors

        With the MLS Cup playoffs now in full swing, it also means that we are beginning to see who is taking home honors at the end of the season. Nashville SC have already seen Maxwell Woledzi win Defender of the Year and Bran Shwake earn Goalkeeper of the Year honors, and they have potential honorees up and down the awards docket alongside the youngest MVP finalist in league history, Cavan Sullivan, who has taken home young player of the year honors. Antoine Griezmann has also won Newcomer of the Year in only half of a season with Orlando City SC.Check out the winners and finalists so far:MLS Goalkeeper of the Year, Brian SchwakeLeading Nashville SC to a record low of 25 goals conceded and tying Tony Meola's record for the most clean sheets in an MLS season with 16, Brian Schwake has taken home Goalkeeper of the Year honors by a landslide, beating out finalists Matt Turner and Roman Bürki. In only his first season as the full-time starter for Nashville, Schwake took the reins and didn't look back, also debuting for the U.S. Men's National Team due to his success. He also set club records for wins, penalty kick saves (three), save percentage (78.4%), and goals against average (0.76).MLS Comeback Player of the Year, Eduard Lowen (San Jose Earthquakes)It's astounding that Eduard Lowen is playing soccer, considering what the few years have looked like for him. In March of this year, his wife Ilona died from brain cancer after they managed through her diagnosis, with Lowen taking time off from the game to support her and her family. He returned to MLS play in April, scoring in his first start of the season for St. Louis City SC, but then was traded to San Jose after the World Cup break. During that time with San Jose, he became an important part of their playoff run with one goal and three assists. 
MLS Young Player of the Year, Cavan Sullivan (Philadelphia Union)Becoming the youngest MVP finalist in league history at only 17, it should come as no surprise that Cavan Sullivan has won Young Player of the Year, beating out the Red Bull New York duo of Julian Hall and Adri Mehmeti. During the World Cup break, Sullivan spent time training with the Union's MLS Next Pro side instead of taking the time off for himself, and the results showed in the second half of the season as he helped lead the Union into a playoff spot. With nine goals and 14 assists (including secondary assists), no teenager has ever been involved in more goals in a season than Sullivan, and it has also led to his first cap with the United States men's national team, where he was able to grab his first goal against Mexico. If this is the tip of the iceberg, we're in for something special, considering that this has been a banner year for young players in MLS, with more minutes being given to teenagers than ever before. The future is in good hands as the kids are leveling up each day.MLS Newcomer of the Year, Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City SC)With Guilherme receiving MVP votes to become a finalist for the award, it was going to take a special performance for someone else to win Newcomer of the Year, and joining Orlando City SC, Antoine Griezmann did just that. Prior to his arrival, this was a team floundering below the playoff line after moving on from manager Oscar Pareja. In only a half-season, he came in and scored 14 goals and assisted eight more as the first player ever to produce 20 goal contributions in only half a season, while turning this team into contenders. It's going to be tough in the playoffs for Griezmann to overcome the defense, but considering what he has already done with the squad, there's no reason why Orlando should be counted out with the Frenchman next to Justin Ellis.
MLS Defender of the Year, Maxwell Woledzi (Nashville SC)En route to setting a points record with 77 points to win the Supporters' Shield, Nashville SC were also led by a record-setting defense that only let the ball into the back of the net 25 times in an entire campaign. That success was rewarded with all three finalists for Defender of the Year coming from Nashville, but it's their newest signing that took home the award. Joining from Norwegian club Fredrikstad ahead of the season, Woledzi didn't need much time to adjust, appearing in every regular-season match and helping Nashville build from the back to maintain possession. It was a team effort to tie the MLS clean sheet record with 17 during the season, so it's only natural for one of their defenders to get the honors this season.Landon Donovan MLS MVP finalistsEvander (FC Cincinnati)Guilherme (Houston Dynamo FC)Lionel Messi (Inter Miami)Hany Mukhtar (Nashville SC)Cavan Sullivan (Philadelphia Union)Sigi Schmid MLS Coach of the Year finalistsB.J. Callaghan (Nashville SC)Yoann Damet (St. Louis City SC)Jesper Sorensen (Vancouver Whitecaps)MLS Humanitarian of the Year finalistsPaul Arriola (Seattle Sounders)Andrew Farrell (New England Revolution)Telasco Segovia (Inter Miami)Mason Stajduhar (Real Salt Lake)Brad Stuver (Austin FC)
